transcript:
HEADER:
Date: 2026-02-12 14:30 PST
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Ari Gupta (Redwood AE), Maya Rosen (Redwood SE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood Solutions), Jenna Ortiz (QuarryTech ML), Marcus Li (QuarryTech Platform), Priya Nair (QuarryTech Product), Ravi Sundar (QuarryTech SRE)

AUTO-SUMMARY (auto gen sometimes messy): quick recap of week 1, KV front-door was lower than expected, explored prompt reuse but canonicalization not yet applied, agreed to run targeted bench and tune TTLs.

00:00 Ari Gupta: alright everyone thanks for joining, um this is Ari from Redwood, well try to keep to 45 mins but we have 52 so good to go, quick roundtable - who wants to start with updates from QuarryTech?
00:12 Jenna Ortiz: hey all, Jenna here. We ran the first two days of traffic through the pilot routing, overall look is that our KV hit rate sits around 22 percent across the pool, which is lower than the 50 plus percent we hypothesized. There's a lot of scatter by endpoint though, some search-like endpoints are higher.
00:34 Marcus Li: yeah to add on, the traffic shape is spiky, and we have a long tail of unique prompts. We're seeing a mix of short user prompts plus longer internal prompts, so prefix reuse is inconsistent. We did try the naive prefix folding patch last night but couldn't roll it wide because of concerns about changing prompt semantics.
00:59 Maya Rosen: right, when you say prefix folding, are you deduplicating identical leading tokens only, or are you normalizing the whole prompt? those are different operations and have different safety implications.
01:14 Jenna Ortiz: current naive approach is exact string prefix equality, nothing semantic. So small typos or added punctuation break reuse.
01:28 Ari Gupta: ok that makes sense, so the low hit rate is mostly a signal processing problem not a capacity problem. There are 3 levers we usually look at: canonicalization/normalization, TTL and eviction policy, and session affinity / sticky routing.
01:44 Priya Nair: can you remind us of how session affinity would help? we were a bit fuzzy on that.
01:51 Maya Rosen: sure. Session affinity keeps a user's recent kv entries on the same serving cluster which increases local hit rates for short lived conversational sessions. It's lower risk because you don't rewrite prompts; you just increase locality of cached keys. But it won't help across users or truly unique prompts.
02:10 Marcus Li: our concern is memory pressure on the dedicated pods, if we do sticky session we might need to scale the cluster. There are cost tradeoffs.
02:22 Diego Alvarez: yep and we measured token cost on sample traffic — adding session affinity shifted effective cache hit to ~35% in a short run but increased GPU mem usage by ~12 percent in that test.
02:40 Ari Gupta: good concrete numbers, that helps. Jenna, do you have the distribution by endpoint? any endpoints that bubble up as quick wins?
02:48 Jenna Ortiz: yes, our conversation-summary endpoint has a high prefix reuse — around 61 percent with identical headings. Query expansion endpoints are lower, ~8 to 12 percent. I think we should target the high-reuse endpoints first for prefix folding.
03:07 Priya Nair: ok that sounds like a prioritized approach — pilot the aggressive normalization on conv-summary and keep safe rules elsewhere.
03:18 Ari Gupta: propose plan: 1) canonicalization rules for conv-summary only (strip punctuation, lowercase, short token aliasing), 2) short TTL bump for session-affinity on conv-summary route to 30s from 10s, 3) eviction policy: lru but hold hot-prefixes in pinned hot set for 60s. We can test that via canary with 5% traffic.
03:42 Marcus Li: can we simulate that with our replay logs first? we don't want to risk user-facing regressions.
03:50 Maya Rosen: yes we can run a replay-based bench in our env; Jenna and Marcus if you can provide a 48 hour log export we will run both replay sim and live canary. Sim will estimate hit‑rate uplift and cost delta.
04:05 Jenna Ortiz: ok we'll get logs, small note — some logs have PII redacted, hope that still exercises prefix reuse patterns.
04:13 Ari Gupta: okay noted, we can work with redacted data; we mostly need the token sequences not PII fields.
04:22 Ravi Sundar: security question, any of the canonicalization rules or prefix folding change where we write data? are we storing more user-derived keys in the cache?
04:30 Diego Alvarez: short answer: the cache keys are deterministic hashes of canonicalized prompts; we do not change persistence semantics. Keys are ephemeral and TTL-bound. For private deployments we can point at your KMS for keying; nothing leaves customer region in Private mode.
04:48 Priya Nair: what's the rollback plan if the normalization causes semantic shift? say summary changes meaning.
04:55 Maya Rosen: we do canary at 5% with auto-fallback; plus we keep eval prompts and run automatic semantic-similarity checks on outputs. If we detect quality regressions beyond threshold we'll rollback to baseline. We'll share the canary playbook doc.
05:14 Ari Gupta: good. Diego you had cost modeling numbers?
05:18 Diego Alvarez: yes quick snapshot — baseline token cost per 1m requests was $1,200 (example), with naive prefix-fold we saw cost reduce by ~18% in the conv-summary group. Session affinity netted 9% reduction in tokens but added the 12% GPU mem overhead which roughly maps to ~6% infra cost increase. So combined approach yields net ~10 to 12% savings in our sim. I'll put the full math in the spreadsheet.
05:48 Marcus Li: this is helpful. Do you have p95 latency impact? we're sensitive to tail latency spikes.
05:54 Maya Rosen: p50 improved slightly with higher cache hits, p95 was stable in our bench — but note session affinity increased variability on pod-level when autoscaling wasn't tuned. With correct autoscaling rules p95 remains within SLO.
06:12 Priya Nair: for the canonicalization we discussed — what exact transforms are safe? examples?
06:18 Maya Rosen: strip punctuation, map common contractions, lowercase, collapse repeated whitespace, normalize dates to tokens like _DATE_. We avoid semantic rewriting like shortening or sentence summarization.
06:30 Jenna Ortiz: a big practical wrinkle: our front end sometimes injects tracking tokens in prompts, that kills reuse. Any way to strip those safely?
06:38 Ari Gupta: yep we can add a rule to drop known tracking headers or a regex filter. We should do it carefully and have a whitelist.
06:46 Priya Nair: what's the expected lift if we aggressively strip tracking tokens?
06:50 Diego Alvarez: our rough sim shows another 12 to 18 percent hit rate improvement on targeted endpoints, but it's very dependent on how prevalent those tokens are.
07:01 Marcus Li: ok let's capture a test: a) run conv-summary canonicalization + strip trackers, b) run session-affinity on conv-summary only, c) compare to baseline. We'll want p50/p95, token cost, GPU mem delta, and qualitative output checks.
07:20 Ari Gupta: agreed. Action items summarized in the doc and will post to spreadsheet. For the bench we have two modes: replay sim (no user risk) and live canary (5% traffic) — both necessary.
07:31 Jenna Ortiz: quick question on metrics: what's the definition of KV hit rate you use? local-hits only or cluster-wide?
07:36 Maya Rosen: good call — we report both. Our headline is cluster-wide hit rate; we also give node-local hit rate which is what session-affinity affects most. We'll include both in the bench.
07:48 Priya Nair: nice. Any concerns on privacy or compliance with our SSO requirements?
07:53 Ari Gupta: none from changes we propose. We will not send raw PII to Redwood in hosted mode if you don't want; for the pilot you can run replay locally in Private or give redacted logs. We already shared the SOC2 summary earlier.
08:07 Marcus Li: ok, timeline wise, can you get config draft by next Tue? we want to schedule the replay run mid-week.
08:12 Ari Gupta: yes Ari: will share config and explainer by Tue 2/17. Maya and Diego will run initial sims and post results by Fri 2/20. Jenna and Marcus will provide logs by Mon 2/16.
08:24 Priya Nair: final Q: what's the criteria to expand pilot to 20%?
08:29 Maya Rosen: we suggested expansion rules: >40% cluster-wide lift on targeted endpoints OR no regressed evals at 99% confidence and latency within 10% of baseline p95. We'll document exact thresholds.
08:46 Ari Gupta: excellent. Any other business?
08:50 Jenna Ortiz: none from me. Thanks folks.
08:53 Ari Gupta: thanks all, recap we'll share config, logs from QuarryTech, run two benches, sync next week. I'll send calendar.
08:59 END OF RECORDING

NOTES ON TRANSCRIPTION: some words got auto-corrected, proper nouns like "QuarryTech" sometimes transcribed as "QueryTech" in the auto notes, timestamps are approximate. There are a few overlaps and crosstalk near 03:00-03:20.
